svg.title: Four Checks Before Capital Moves
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-05-statutory-risk-preflight; chart type: decision_tree; title: Four Checks Before Capital Moves; subtitle: Every failed branch stops the bid or the proposed enforcement step.; chapter number: 5; epistemic tag: operating_framework; assumptions note: Read these as ordered checks: passing advances to the next check; failing produces the stated stop action. Numeric values are layout weights, not probabilities. Re-run relevant checks before enforcement because bankruptcy, title, and statutory facts can change after purchase.; caption: Local auction eligibility, rate limits, notice procedures, and redemption rights control the investment. A successful auction bid does not resolve title defects or authorize retaining another party's protected surplus.; stages: label: Eligibility and auction mechanics; value: Pass documented authority; otherwise do not bid; numeric value: 1.0; detail: Verify bidder registration, deposits, payment deadlines, asset type, and rate or premium rules against the current county packet and governing statute. If any material rule is unresolved, remove the parcel from the live bid list.; label: Title, stays, and federal interests; value: Pass counsel review; otherwise suspend affected action; numeric value: 1.0; detail: Review recorded liens, ownership, access, and bankruptcy status. Counsel evaluates 11 U.S.C. section 362 and federal lien notice or redemption issues under 26 U.S.C. section 7425; a recorder search alone does not establish that enforcement may proceed.; label: Redemption, notice, and surplus; value: Pass lawful procedure; otherwise redesign the exit; numeric value: 1.0; detail: Map the jurisdiction's redemption period, required notices, foreclosure procedure, and surplus distribution. Apply Tyler v. Hennepin County, 598 U.S. 631 (2023), to the relevant government-taking issue without assuming identical rules for every private certificate.; label: Loss capacity and bid economics; value: Pass funded downside; otherwise reduce bid or reject; numeric value: 1.0; detail: Stress delayed redemption, unusable collateral, subsequent taxes, counsel expense, and capital loss. Reject positions whose loss exposure or cash demands exceed funded reserves; a large statutory rate cannot repair defective collateral or an excessive premium.
